home.tagline: Une table familiale au bord de la mer — Cala San Vicente, depuis 2016

heritage.subtitle: d'aventure familiale néerlandaise sur une île espagnole

quote.body: Partager votre repas et passer du temps avec vos proches tout en profitant de la vue sur la plage et la mer — c'est notre idée du paradis.

act3.headline: Là où la route s'arrête et la mer commence
act3.body: Cala San Vicente se trouve à l'extrême nord d'Ibiza, au-delà du dernier virage. La route s'arrête ici. Depuis la terrasse du restaurant, la crique s'ouvre sur l'eau turquoise et les falaises intactes d'Es Molí.

act4.headline: Là où les histoires se posent et la table attend
act4.body: Notre carte, notre cuisine, notre maison — vous êtes arrivés.

act5.headline: Moderne, biologique, hyperlocal
act5.intro: Cinq plats signature de la côte méditerranéenne et d'ailleurs, préparés avec les produits de notre ferme zéro-km et de partenaires de confiance en Espagne et en Italie.

act5b.headline: Five places, one table
act5b.intro: Our pantry is a quiet map of the Mediterranean — Galician beef, our own zero-km farm five minutes from the kitchen, buffalo mozzarella from a single dairy outside Naples, mezze that travels from Beirut, and the catch our captain lands at the cove that morning.

act6.headline: Anchor your boat — we deliver to the cove
act6.body: Captains, sail in. Drop anchor at Cala San Vicente, message us with your VHF or WhatsApp, and our skiff brings the table to you. Lunch, drinks, paella for the whole crew — served on deck or in the sand.
act6.col1Body: On the deck or under the pines. Lunch from 12:30, dinner from 19:00, last booking at 22:00.
act6.col2Body: Drop anchor at Cala San Vicente, ping us on VHF 09 or WhatsApp +34 971 334 273, our skiff comes out within fifteen minutes.

act7.headline: We'll keep your table waiting
act7.body: Whether you arrive by car, by boat, or by long lazy walk along the cliffs — we'll be at the corner of the deck, watching the cove turn from turquoise to gold. Welcome home.
act7.address: Calle del Calo 12, Cala San Vicente, Eivissa

r1.body: An aquarium floor under your feet, a cove view that softens with the sun. The food kept up — every plate read as the place itself.

r2.body: We arrived by boat for lunch. Two hours later we were still at the table, our skipper was at the bar, and nobody seemed to want to leave.

r3.body: The Friesian Tomahawk for two is the most honest steak I've eaten in Ibiza. The salsa verde — pure cove, pure sea.

menu.headline: Plates born of place
menu.intro: Six small editorial chapters — tapas, starters, mains, salads, desserts, drinks. Hyper-local where we can, sourced with intent everywhere else.

callout.label: Reserve
callout.title: Tables fill fast in season
callout.body: We accept reservations from 12:30 to 23:00. For groups over six, please contact us directly so we can prepare the right corner of the deck.

about.headline: Forty years of Dutch curiosity on a Spanish island
about.intro: From a single van in Figueretes to a beachfront table at the cove — the story of a family that fell in love with Ibiza, learned its kitchens, and stayed.

1985.title: A van, a dog, an idea
1985.body: Tom and Maria Zandwijk arrive in Figueretes with a Volkswagen Bus, a black Labrador called Otto, and the conviction that food can be both Dutch in discipline and Spanish in soul.

2005.title: On the Beach
2005.body: After two decades of seasonal kitchens across the island, the family opens On the Beach in Cala San Vicente — the first table where the menu was as small as the cove itself.

2016.title: The Boat House
2016.body: A renovated boathouse on the same beach, larger crew, the same idea: share food with people you love while the sea decides the time of day.

2025.title: The cove farm
2025.body: Our zero-km farm opens behind the dunes — tomatoes, herbs, leaves and edible flowers walk to the kitchen the same morning.

about.chefBio: Trained in Amsterdam, Madrid and Bangkok, Lieke runs the kitchen with her brother Sven on the pass. Her food reads like a postcard: a paella that nods to Valencia but speaks Mediterranean Ibiza, a curry that travels from Bangkok back to the cove.

chef.headline: Lieke Zandwijk
chef.intro: Daughter of the founders, fifth-year chef de cuisine at The Boat House. Trained across three continents, she runs the pass with her brother Sven.
chef.name: Lieke Zandwijk
chef.pullQuote: I cook the cove first. The plates come second.
chef.body1: Lieke grew up between Amsterdam and Cala San Vicente. The kitchen of her parents' first restaurant in Figueretes is the room where she learned to peel garlic and read the sea — both at once, both seasonally.
chef.body2: After culinary school in Amsterdam she worked the line at Het Bosch, then crossed to Madrid for a year under Dabiz Muñoz at DiverXO, and finally to Bangkok for a season at Gaggan. She came home in 2018 to take the pass at The Boat House.
chef.body3: Her food philosophy is editorial: small menu, deep sourcing, no garnish for garnish's sake. The cove farm — opened by the family in 2025 — is her daily restraint: vegetables that walked to the kitchen the same morning, herbs cut at 11:00 for service at 13:00.
chef.sigPaella: Bomba rice, the morning's catch, sofrito made the day before. Slow until the pan whispers.
chef.sigTomahawk: Galician Friesian, dry-aged fifty days, finished over olive wood, salsa verde from the cove herbs.
chef.sigCurry: Bangkok roots, Mediterranean catch — local sea-bass, prawns from Formentera, kaffir from the farm.
chef.sigLeaves: Cove farm leaves, sherry-wine-vinegar emulsion, citrus segmented at the pass.

gallery.headline: Forty seasons in colour
gallery.intro: Plates, faces, sky, salt. A loose archive of the cove and the table — updated every spring.

press.headline: What others have written
press.intro: Six selected mentions across the past four seasons. The longer archive is in the Sanity CMS — these are the editorial highlights.
press.contactTitle: For interviews, photoshoots, and tasting visits
press.contactBody: We host journalists weekly during shoulder seasons. Send your outlet, the angle, and the dates — we'll arrange a tasting with chef Lieke and a quiet corner of the deck.

contact.headline: Find us, write us, drop anchor
contact.intro: We answer email within the day. For same-day reservations, please call directly — the line is open from 11:00.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.s1Body: The Boat House Ibiza S.L. operates this site at theboathouseibiza.com. Registered office: Calle del Calo 12, 07810 Sant Joan de Labritja, Eivissa.
privacy.s2Body: Reservation requests (name, email, date, party size, message), language preference, anonymous analytics on page visits and scroll depth via Vercel Analytics. We do not run third-party advertising trackers.
privacy.s3Body: Reservation data goes to the front-of-house system (Sevenrooms) to confirm your booking and send a single reminder. Analytics is aggregated, never tied to you personally.
privacy.s4Body: Under EU GDPR you can request access, correction or deletion of your personal data at hello@theboathouseibiza.com. We respond within 30 days.
privacy.s5Body: Reservation records are kept for 24 months for accounting and recurring-guest recognition, then deleted. Analytics is rolled up to monthly aggregates after 13 months.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: We use only cookies that are strictly necessary to make the site work, plus a single anonymised analytics cookie. No advertising, no cross-site tracking.
cookies.r1Purpose: Remembers your selected language across visits.
cookies.r2Purpose: Anonymised page-view counts. Aggregated by Vercel.
cookies.r3Purpose: Holds your reservation form between page loads on /contact.

terms.title: Terms
terms.s1Body: Reservations are confirmed by email. We hold tables for 15 minutes past the booked time. For groups over six, a deposit may be requested — we'll always tell you in writing first.
terms.s2Body: Free up to 24 hours before the booking. Inside 24 hours we may charge a per-person fee of €15 to cover prepped produce. No charge for force-majeure (illness, weather, port closure).
terms.s3Body: Tell us at the time of booking. Our kitchen handles gluten, shellfish, nuts and dairy daily; we cannot guarantee a fully cross-contamination-free environment.
terms.s4Body: The cove and its access path are public. We are not responsible for property left in the parking area or on the public beach. The aquarium-floor section of the deck is accessible; please supervise children.

footer.tagline: A family table by the sea — Cala San Vicente, since 2016.
